- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Not recorded.

Formulation:
Predisposing: Family history of serious illness (father’s bowel cancer).  
Precipitating: Acute gastrointestinal infection causing significant discomfort and functional impairment.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing physical symptoms, limited water/food intake, uncertainty about seriousness, possible maladaptive health anxiety.  
Protective: Adequate insight, willingness to consult healthcare, employment, no reported mental health history.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce worry about current symptoms and cancer risk; resume normal functioning and work.
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide psycho-education on normal course of gastroenteritis, address health anxiety, monitor for escalation.
- Actions (Patient):
  • Follow medical advice for hydration and monitoring red-flag symptoms.  
  • Practice scheduled worry time or relaxation techniques (not yet taught).  
  • Seek review if anxiety worsens or persists after physical recovery.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide clear written information on gastroenteritis versus bowel cancer red flags.  
  • Normalise anxiety response; screen formally for GAD at follow-up.  
  • Consider brief CBT-based interventions or referral to mental health professional if anxiety persists.  

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Not recorded.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of gastroenteritis, hydration, monitoring fever, differentiating acute infection from malignancy concerns.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent diarrhoea > 7 days, blood in stool, weight loss, escalating anxiety interfering with daily life.
- Coping Strategies: Maintain hydration, paced breathing when anxious, limit Internet searching about cancer, contact GP if concerns increase.

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded.
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded.
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently.
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable.
- Review Date: To be scheduled within 2–4 weeks or sooner if symptoms/anxiety escalate.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Health Anxiety / Illness Anxiety Disorder – Likelihood: Medium. Justification: Patient expresses significant worry about bowel cancer despite presentation suggesting acute infection.
- Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety – Likelihood: Medium. Justification: Anxiety temporally related to acute medical stressor and functional impact.
- Generalized Anxiety Disorder – Likelihood: Low. Justification: Anxiety appears situation-specific; chronic pervasive worry not established in transcript.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Suicidal ideation assessment, detailed psychosocial history, substance/alcohol use, sleep pattern, formal anxiety screening, consent documentation, follow-up appointment date.  
● Internal conflicts: DOB conflict (1992 vs age 48 implying ~1975).  
● Transcript quality notes: Primarily a physical-health consultation; limited exploration of mental health; no direct risk inquiries.
